Based on Philip's review: quieter, more native, and a layout that builds itself.

## Look & feel
- **Native window controls:** Windows 11 caption buttons (exact size and glyphs, red close), macOS traffic lights.
- **MENU** lines up with the cover column below it.
- **Quieter header:** smaller title, **artist on its own line** (from tags, or from "Artist - Title" file names), one compact info line, redesigned quick-access tiles on the same grid.
- Volume percentage no longer cut off; nothing overlaps at small window sizes (min. 640 × 240).
- **Display size** setting: Small / Medium / Large / Extra large.

## Layout
- **Customize mode** (MENU or a quick-access button): the + tile and slot controls only appear here. Drag to reorder, set each slot's width (narrow → extra wide), resize the header and waveform with the orange handles.
- **Auto layout:** every plugin has its natural shape (goniometer square, VU 3:2, spectrum wide …) and slots are packed into justified rows that always fill the area. Header and waveform give way before the plugins do when the window gets small.
- **Maximize any plugin:** double-click it (or the ⤢ button) to fill the whole plugin area; Esc restores.

## Plugins
- **VU meter** redesigned as a real meter face: full scale, pivot under a hub cap, stereo L/R pair when the slot is wide.
- **Loudness:** layout adapts to the slot, adds **LRA** (EBU Tech 3342) and **true peak**, and a target you can click through: Streaming −14 / Apple Music −16 / EBU R128 −23 LUFS, with the history graph centred on it.
- **Spectrum:** peak readout (frequency, note, level). Titles and units on every analyzer; L/R labels on Peak/RMS.

## Windows & macOS
- **Taskbar mini player (Windows):** hover the taskbar button for cover, title and progress with ⏮ ⏯ ⏭ buttons. Can be turned off in MENU.
- **Default audio player:** offered once on first start (and in MENU). Windows: Transport registers itself and opens Settings → Default apps on its entry, where you click "Set default" — Windows doesn't allow apps to do this silently. macOS: switches directly.

## Downloads
| Platform | File | How to start |
|---|---|---|
| Windows 10/11 (64-bit) | `Transport-Windows-x64.exe` | Just run it, nothing to install. SmartScreen: *More info → Run anyway* (not code-signed yet). |
| macOS 11+ (Apple Silicon & Intel) | `Transport-macOS.zip` | Unzip, right-click → **Open** the first time (not notarised yet). |
| Linux x64 | `Transport-Linux-x64.tar.gz` | Extract and run `./Transport`. |

## Not yet verified on a real desktop
The taskbar mini player and the default-app registration compile and are built on the Windows API as documented, but couldn't be clicked through in CI. Please report anything odd.
